newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS-BTP, Bund vol slips, iron butterfly trades.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS-BTP, Bund vol slips, iron butterfly trades.

text.p: Implied volatility of BTP and Bund options slipped on Friday ahead of key U.S. employment data later, and volatility is likely to fall further, options traders said.
"We are a little bit lower, after opening a bit higher on the back of yesterday's sell-off in Bunds," said one broker from a UK brokerage.
"When the future stabilised, volatility ticked down."
September Bund futures dropped to a low of 102.90 late on Thursday, rattled by the weakness of the mark. The contract closed at 103.03, and was up 0.05 at 103.08 at 1116 GMT.

Volatility of September Bund options exercisable into the September future was quoted at 5.09-5.26 percent by 1100 GMT, the UK broker said. October options exercisable into the December future were quoted at 5.13-5.26 percent, November at 5.16-5.24 percent and December at 5.17-5.27 percent.
In BTP options, September volatility was quoted at 6.62-6.66 percent, against a close of 6.85 percent, and December at 6.98 percent.
U.S. July employment data will be released at 1230 GMT. Non-farm payrolls are set to rise by 193,000, compared with a 217,000 gain in June, according to a Reuters survey.
"Volatility will come off across the board ahead of the data," said one broker from a U.S. bank. "Some players have been setting up their positions beforehand."
A large iron butterfly trade in Bund options was a feature of Friday's session, brokers said. An iron butterfly involves the purchase of a straddle and sale of a strangle.
In Friday's iron butterfly trade, one player sold September Bund puts at the 102.50 strike, bought puts and calls at the 103.00 strike and sold calls at the 103.50 strike.
The trade assumes range trading for the contract between 102.50 and 103.50. Such trades are popular with brokers, as they receive commission for each leg of the transaction.
"It's a Cadillac trade," said the UK broker. "It's low risk for the client, and the broker drives home in a Cadillac."
By 1130 GMT, 3,120 contracts had changed hands in the 102.50 puts, 3,441 in the 103.00 calls, 2,151 in the 103.00 puts, and 3,000 contracts in the 103.50 calls.
Volatility is likely to fall later in the session, due to options time decay, brokers said.
"Once we've got the figures out of the way, volatility will come off ahead of the weekend, unless the numbers are very dramatic," the UK broker said.
